ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Clinical Nutrition Referral — Mahatma Gandhi

code.originalText: Primary care visit for high home blood pressure readings in a thin, vegetarian 70-year-old man

text.paragraph: Nutrition assessment for a 70-year-old lacto-vegetarian man with stage 2 hypertension, BMI 17.1, and vitamin B12 and D deficiency, who intends to keep a seven-day fast next month. Please assess his nutritional status, set energy and protein targets within his diet, advise on vitamin B12, vitamin D, calcium, sodium, and potassium, and write a safe plan for the fast and for refeeding that respects his decision to fast. [S]
Urgency: Soon, within four weeks and before the planned fast. [S]

list.item: What is his nutritional status, and does he meet criteria for malnutrition?
What energy and protein targets do you advise, and how can he meet them within his lacto-vegetarian diet with goat's milk?
How should vitamin B12, vitamin D, and calcium be managed, given his diet and his low bone mass risk?
What sodium and potassium advice fits his blood pressure and his diet?
What plan do you advise for the seven-day fast and for refeeding afterwards, given his refeeding risk?

text.paragraph: Lifelong lacto-vegetarian by conviction, with goat's milk and curd, fruit, nuts, vegetables, and whole grains; no eggs, meat, fish, tea, coffee, or alcohol; little salt; walks 5 km daily; fasts for reasons of conscience. Stage 2 hypertension: 168/94 mmHg at intake, home average 162/92, ECG voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; started amlodipine 2.5 mg; a thiazide avoided because of fasting and low weight. Weight 46.6 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 17.1; Mini Nutritional Assessment 20 (at risk). Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, MCV 99 fL, vitamin B12 238 pg/mL with methylmalonic acid 0.48 umol/L, folate 17.5 ng/mL, ferritin 46 ng/mL, albumin 3.9 g/dL, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 19 ng/mL, phosphate 3.4 and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, eGFR 94. DXA ordered. He has full decision-making capacity and has decided to fast for seven days, taking water with a little salt and citrus juice [S]

list.item: Home blood pressure readings in the 160s, and a wish to control them with as little medicine as possible while keeping his diet. [S]
He intends to keep a seven-day fast of conscience next month and asks for help to keep it as safely as possible, without being asked to give it up. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Mahatma Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869. [D]

According to his health file for 1924 to 1947, kept at the National Gandhi Museum, his blood pressure readings were as high as 194/130 on October 26, 1937, and 220/110 on February 19, 1940, and other readings in between reached about 170/110 and 180/105. [D]

In March 1927 his blood pressure was high throughout the day, and physicians' statements published in the Bombay Chronicle of March 29, 1927, warned of a danger of apoplexy from high blood pressure due to continuous overwork and advised absolute rest in a cool climate; on May 2, 1927, his blood pressure was found to be normal. [D]

To lower his blood pressure he placed a mud poultice on his abdomen, applied a mud bandage to his head in summer, and took sarpagandha, an Ayurvedic preparation of Rauwolfia serpentina; a physician's account says he took garlic daily after it was suggested as a remedy. [D]

His electrocardiogram and oscillograph reports of October 27 and 28, 1937, found diminished arterial elasticity, a fairly good myocardium, and slight enlargement of the heart; the report of February 19, 1940, found slight myocarditis, normal for his age, with cardiovascular degeneration arrested. [D]
A basal metabolic test on April 30, 1939, recorded his height as 5 feet 5 inches and his weight as 46.7 kg. [D]

During a fast at Rajkot in March 1939, health bulletins reported his blood pressure as 170/110 on March 4 with weakness of the heart and swelling of the feet, and 180/110 on March 5, with a loss of two pounds; a urine test on March 5 showed acetone in large amounts; he broke the fast on the afternoon of March 7 with fruit juices, honey, and jaggery. [D]

He kept a vegetarian diet; he took a vow not to drink cow's or buffalo milk and later, when ill, accepted goat's milk on medical advice; in Key to Health he wrote that experience had taught him that a vegetarian diet must include milk and milk products such as curd, butter, and ghee. [D]

Earlier illnesses in the cited summary include pleurisy in London in 1914, acute dysentery in 1918 and 1929, an operation for piles in 1919, an operation for acute appendicitis on January 12, 1924, and malaria in 1925 and 1936. [D]

He walked about 18 km a day for nearly 40 years, about 79,000 km during his campaigns from 1913 to 1948; his daily routine at Sevagram included a morning walk of about 5 km, kitchen and cleaning work, and spinning. [D]

Blood sugar measurements of 41 in January 1936, 71.4 in December 1937, and 115 in April 1938 are recorded in his health file; his cholesterol readings were within the normal range and his hemoglobin was 14.96 g/dL. [D]
He preached against tea and coffee, along with drugs, tobacco, and alcohol. [D]

text.paragraph: 3 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.

list.item: Essential hypertension, stage 2, with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented high blood pressure: active, confirmed [S]
Underweight (BMI 17.1) from a long-standing, chosen lean lacto-vegetarian diet and periodic fasting; at risk of malnutrition, with high refeeding risk after a fast: active, confirmed [S]

Blood pressure plan agreed with him: home readings twice a day, sodium under 1500 to 2300 mg a day, potassium-rich fruit and vegetables, his daily walk, and amlodipine started at 2.5 mg; a thiazide is avoided for now because of his low weight, fasting, and the risk of low sodium and potassium. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Indian guidelines on hypertension-IV (2019) (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and osteoporosis monographs (2026) [S]

Falls and orthostatic checks: lying and standing blood pressure at every visit, extra fluids in hot weather, and a yearly Timed Up and Go. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and osteoporosis monographs (2026) [S]

CMID hypertension monitoring: blood pressure and weight every visit; a metabolic panel, lipids, urine albumin, and HbA1c yearly; baseline ECG and echocardiogram for stage 2; a yearly eye examination, depression screen, and cardiovascular risk estimate. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and osteoporosis monographs (2026) [S]
